text:
ella: Heads-up — seeing tail latency regressions for short sequences when a few long sessions are active. profiling shows batch formation delay and queueing spike under KV pressure.

sam: Can you paste the quick numbers? p50/p95/p99 split?

ella: quick summary: short seq p99 ~420ms baseline, during green-zone long sessions p99 jumps to ~680ms. p50 ~22ms -> ~38ms. GPU kernel idle cycles up. KV hit rate drops ~6%.

sam: My hunch: our continuous batcher coalesces too aggressively, forming batches that favor long-token requests. Thinking about a "stride window" allocator: allocate slots in a round-robin across lanes (long/short/tenant) to avoid long-tail grabs.

sam: Proposed config snippet (experiment):
```
batcher.window_ms: 6
batcher.max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
allocator.strategy: "stride"
allocator.stride_size: 4
allocator.short_boost_factor: 1.8
allocator.max_wait_ms: 40
kv.prefetch_prefix_ms: 2
```

ryan: Ran a small sandbox run with stride=4 on a 4-tenant mix (heavy long-threads). Results vs current: short p99 420ms -> 150ms, short p95 110ms -> 42ms. long p99 increased from 320ms -> 332ms (≈+12ms). overall GPU utilization similar. starved_tenants (threshold wait>200ms) 9->1.

marta: Nice! Did you check KV warmup effect? If we preempt long batches we might lose KV locality and hurt throughput later. Need to ensure per-tenant KV lanes or prefix cache TTL bump.

ryan: I tracked kv_hit_rate: baseline 92% -> stride run 89% at steady state, transient dips to 83% during peak long churn but recovers after 30s. Net token/sec same ±3%. So slight KV cost but much better fairness.

ella: Good trade-off. We should try smaller window_ms (4ms) and a conservative short_boost_factor (1.2) to reduce KV churn. Also add a tiny pre-alloc credit for short lanes so they aren't entirely at mercy of alignment.

sam: Agreed. New experiment matrix: window_ms [4,6,8], stride_size [2,4,8], short_boost [1.2,1.5,1.8], max_wait_ms [30,40,60]. We'll record metrics: short_p99, long_p99, kv_hit_rate, starved_tenants, tokens_per_sec, kernel_switch_rate.

marta: Add a telemetry tag: batch_alloc_policy so we can roll back in console. And a gauge for "max_pending_time_by_tenant".

ops-bot: deploy-canary started: eng-runtime-canary/stride-experiment v3 -> 10% hosts.

ryan: Canary live. Early telemetry (2m): short p99 down ~60%, long p99 steady, kv hit dip -3%. no OOMs.

ella: OK let's let it run for 30m across 10% then escalate to 50% if stable. I'll draft a short runbook: rollback if short_p99 rises or tokens/sec drops >8% or kv_hit_rate <80%.

sam: runbook acked. Also logging note: add per-batch label "alloc_reason" (stride/fastpath/legacy) so we can trace regressions back to allocator decisions.

marta: FYI also noticed with stride_size>6 we see an uptick in kernel swapping on A100s due to larger multi-seq combined state — limit stride<=4 on those instances.

ella: Great catch. I'll add instance-aware caps. Thanks all, will post results after 30m window. :thumbsup:
